relevance_note: Case report of a developmentally delayed female with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency, with individual-level detail: "The proband was compound heterozygous for pathogenic ALDH5A1 mutations (p.(Asn418IlefsTer39); maternal; p.(Gly409Asp); paternal)".
method_note: Read the whole Markdown full text (case report, one patient plus her parents). I transcribed Table 1 by hand; no script was used; no ' / ' stacked cells occur in this paper. In Table 1 the continuation rows repeat no 'Family member' cell; I read the rows after 'Mother' and after 'Father' as belonging to those two people (ALDH5A1 row + MECP2 row each). The proband's two ALDH5A1 variants are each printed 'Hz, AR' while the abstract calls the proband 'compound heterozygous'; I recorded zygosity 'heterozygous' on each variant row and note the compound-heterozygous state here. Variant class: the authors print 'Protein termination' in the table Comment column but never name a class for the ALDH5A1 variants, so variant_type_as_stated is 'not reported' for them (never derived from the HGVS string); MECP2 p.Arg255* is called a 'nonsense mutation' in the abstract. Pathogenicity 'pathogenic' comes from the abstract sentence that names the proband; the table note 'all variants are predicted to be pathogenic' was not used because it is a general statement. Both parents are in scope as tested relatives (heterozygous carriers of one ALDH5A1 variant each); their MECP2 cells read 'Not detected', so no MECP2 variant row was made for them. Contradiction/time-dependence: the EEG was 'interpreted as normal' at 28 months but a follow-up at 36 months showed 'diffuse slowing indicative of encephalopathy'; I emitted both phenotypic_features rows (excluded at 28 months, observed at 36 months) and scored the checklist item 'EEG abnormality (background slowing or epileptiform activity)' as observed. Checklist items left 'not reported' although the paper gives related wording: intellectual disability (paper says 'global developmental delay' / 'developmentally delayed'), ataxia (paper says 'gait anomalies'/'apraxia'), autism spectrum disorder (paper only says she lacks the 'characteristic social delays'), cerebral or cerebellar atrophy (paper says only 'suspicion for mild, diffuse parenchymal volume loss'). The paper's counts of 'previous SSADHD DBSs (n = 7)' and '2,831 archival DBS samples' are comparison/control samples from earlier work, not patients of this study, and were not extracted. publications.cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = false and has span null: the paper never states that its patient was published earlier (Hogema et al. (2001) and Christodoulou & Ho (2012) are cited only for variant descriptions), so no verbatim quote can support the false value. The proband is labelled 'patient' because the paper's own word for her is the role word 'proband', which is not a label.
